text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.
LONDON - UK shares finished higher for the first time in seven sessions as renewed bid speculation swirled around the dealing rooms in London's "Square Mile" financial district.
A firmer look to Wall Street also gave the market a much needed boost.
The FTSE 100, which had dropped in the previous six trading days, ended 19.1 points higher to 4,576.2.

FRANKFURT - German shares posted minor gains amid relief that the Bundesbank and Bonn seemed close to reconciliation in their spat over asset revaluation, easing fears of a soft start for monetary union.

The 30-share DAX ended the bourse session up 11.19 points at 3,673.03 points, buoyed by selective interest in individual shares -- most notably airline Deutsche Lufthansa. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,684.60. Up 33.01 points.

PARIS - French shares close more than two percent higher, bolstered by relief at the composition of France's Socialist-led government. It includes a known quantity as finance minister, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, and assigns only one big portfolio, transport, to the Communists.
The CAC-40 index closed up 55.48, or 2.11 percent, at 2,690.85.
ZURICH - Swiss shares posted their third consecutive record close which was partially due to merger and spin-off rumours in the financial sector, dealer said.
The prospect for low interest rates, a firming tendency in the U.S. dollar and early Wall Street highs also bolsted prices.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 12.7 points, or 0.24 percent, to 5,251.2. and the broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 14.28 points, or 0.43 percent, to 3,327.99.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended lower, bruised by profit-taking after three days of gains, brokers said. They added however that certain shares posted healthy gains and market sentiment continued to be fairly bullish.
The 225-share Nikkei average shed 123.41 points or 0.60 percent to finish at 20,488.15. Its June futures slipped 80 yen to finish at 20,470.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed modestly lower after a day of choppy trading, with profit-taking alternating with bargain-hunting and index futures related buying.
The Hang Seng Index fell 36.06 points, or 0.24 percent, to end at 14,795.52 after moving between 14,709.03 and 14,914.28.
SYDNEY - The Australian stock market ended near its lows after sitting in negative territory all day in line with an easier U.S. market and softer commodities.
The benchmark All Ordinaries Index closed down 11.7 points at 2,604.2.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares rallied for the fourth consecutive day on heavy foreign and local buying, which sent packaging stock Malbak surging and the financial and all-share indexes to fresh highs.

Dealers said that renewed talk of an interest rate cut in the third quarter of the year propped up banking shares, which together with other heavyweights also received a boost from futures-related arbitrage deals.
The financial index soared over 122 points or 1.3 percent, helping the industrial index gain 41.5 points to 8,469.9. The industrial index has put on over 220 points so far this week.
